description:
FILED s469bf (Opus) while attributing the companion ROW DIFF of the re/ comp/
run/ dirs.  PRE-EXISTING; the HARNESS, not the product.

THE MECHANISM.  perl's own t/test.pl builds a temp name out of the PID:

    sub tempfile {                                   # t/test.pl:1080
        my $try_prefix = (-d "t" ? "t/" : "") . "tmp_" . _num_to_alpha($$);
        ... $try = $try_prefix . "_" . _num_to_alpha($count) ...
    }
    # and DECLARES the shape:  $::tempfile_regexp = 'tmp_[A-Z]+_[A-Z]+'

PCL's transpilable stub (perl-tests/t/test.pl:340-349) answers a completely
different spelling:

    sub tempfile {
        my $try = "/tmp/pcl-test-$$-$tempfile_counter";
        ...
    }

A test that INTERPOLATES the name into its description therefore emits two
descriptions that can never pair.  t/run/cloexec.t is the measured case
(lines 85 and 105, `ok( -f $tmpfile2, "tmpfile '$tmpfile2' exists" )`): the
two perl rows come back `(missing)` and PCL's two identical assertions come
back as `*extra*` rows, i.e. FOUR diverging rows in a file whose counts
(16/6) match the snapshot exactly.  Both of those assertions PASS on both
sides — the divergence is entirely in the NAME.

WHAT s469bf DID (the instrument half only).  `PclTapAlign::rowkey_desc` now
normalises `/tmp/pcl-test-<pid>-<n>` to `/tmp/pcl-test-TMPFILE` beside the
`tmp_[A-Z]+_[A-Z]+` rule it already had for perl's spelling, so the four rows
are STABLE and blessable (they moved every single run before: /tmp/pcl-test-
64955-2 -> /tmp/pcl-test-338873-2, tmp_CQZP_C -> tmp_JVEJ_...).  Guards:
tools/t/tap-align.t (+2 rows, the positive and the negative "a path that
merely starts with /tmp/pcl-test- is not a tempfile name").  run/cloexec.t's
four rows are blessed into baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv with this cause.

WHAT IS LEFT (this task).  Make the stub answer perl's SHAPE, so the rows
PAIR and leave the diverging set altogether:

    my $try_prefix = (-d "t" ? "t/" : "") . "tmp_" . _num_to_alpha($$);

Expected gain: run/cloexec.t 16/6 -> 18/4 (the two assertions already pass;
they are only counted as failures because the descriptions do not meet), and
the same for any future test that quotes a tempfile name.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE HERE, and what it costs:
  * perl-tests/t/test.pl is the HARNESS.  CLAUDE.md's WHAT-TO-RUN-WHEN table
    makes a harness change the most expensive row in the table: full sweep +
    `--all --quick` on BOTH populations, because every one of the ~640 files
    in the two suites loads it.  That is a session, not a filler.
  * the two spellings are not interchangeable: perl's name is RELATIVE (it is
    created in the cwd, which for the companion runner is the shadow t/),
    PCL's is an absolute /tmp path.  Anything that opens the name with a
    relative path, or that cleans up by unlinking it, has to keep working.
  * `_num_to_alpha` would have to exist in the stub (perl's is ~15 lines and
    is pure perl, so PCL transpiles it), and the collision loop (commit
    07c0896, "tempfile() must not hand back a name that already exists",
    task #25) must survive.

ACCEPTANCE: run/cloexec.t reaches 18/4 with its four rows GONE from
baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv; the sweep TOTAL does not move; the `--all
--quick` companion shows no other file changing on the tempfile name.

RELATED: #1082 (the volatile row-key class this belongs to), #993 (the audit),
tools/lib/PclTapAlign.pm's rowkey_desc comment block.
subject: PCL's test.pl `tempfile()` stub spells the name differently from perl's, so every row that QUOTES a tempfile name is unpairable (run/cloexec.t: 2 (missing) + 2 *extra*)
